differs: Water in the End, where vanilla has none: broad, still, shallow lakes spread across the islands on every stretch of level ground and run together into wide sheets, held in by their shores so they never spill into the void; springs break out of the higher ground and pour down into them, and here and there a spring at the very edge of an island sends a column of water falling into the void; clay and sand beds lit by sea pickles, sand shores with dry grass, deep blue water, and calm.
